lastCommit.message:
OTA-1879 — the roll leaves room to read

The owner played a fight on a Pixel 10 Pro XL — a large, tall phone — and the
combat-roll surface still pressed the transcript off the screen. His ruling was a
conservation order, not a brief for a redesign: SAME LOOK, SAME INFORMATION, SAME
INTERACTION, SMALLER FOOTPRINT. The composition is approved and is not touched.

THE FORENSICS FOUND NO GROWTH TO REMOVE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. DiceRoller
contains no `Dimensions`, no `useWindowDimensions`, no `useUiScale`, no
percentage height and no aspect ratio, and `useUiScale` clamps to 1 at width
≥ 390 — so a wide phone earns neither capping nor vertical relief and the panel
is the SAME height on a 4.7" screen and a 6.8" one. It was simply ~368pt at the
post-roll peak, of which ~112pt (30%) was AIR: the container's 14pt padding
nested inside the card's own 14pt padding, five 8pt gaps, and four small margins
doubling gaps they already sat beside. The transcript is the only flexible region
on that screen (OTA-179), so it paid for every one of those pixels.

SO THIS IS SPACING AND NOTHING ELSE. Every font size, weight, letter-spacing,
colour, border, radius, word, element, handler and timing is what shipped. No row
was merged, nothing was removed, no type shrank, there is no reduced variant and
no device branch. Option B — pairing Total with the verdict and the header with
the roll label — was offered in the forensics and the owner declined it; it is
not here.

THE NUMBERS COME FROM ONE MODEL WITH THE LIVE FONT SIZES ON BOTH SIDES, so what
they compare is spacing and can be nothing else:

  attack post-roll — the peak    366.6 → 326.6    −40.0pt   −10.9%
  attack pre-roll                277.3 → 240.3    −37.0pt
  damage pre-roll                275.8 → 231.8    −44.0pt
  damage post-roll               343.7 → 306.7    −37.0pt

⚠ They are DERIVED, not device-measured: nothing in this component sets a
`lineHeight`, so a text row is the font's own line box and the absolute values
carry a metric assumption. The DIFFERENCE is what the package promised, and the
suite brackets it rather than pinning a decimal.

THE BUTTON'S NUMBER IS SET BY THE LANDING JUMP, NOT BY TASTE. OTA-255 added
`advancingHint` so the panel would not move when a roll auto-resolves, and its
comment says it takes the ROLL button's footprint. It never did — 39.6 against
48.8, a ~9pt jump every time dice landed. Matching by RAISING the hint would have
grown the post-roll state, which is the peak this package exists to reduce, so
the button came down to the hint instead: 40.8, within 1.2pt. That leaves the
ROLL face ~41pt where the guidance wants ~44 for a finger, so the TOUCH target is
restored with a hitSlop — 52.8pt to the finger, 40.8 to the eye. The press
contract is untouched, and the slop is capped in test so it cannot become a way
of smuggling the visible height back.

AND THE CARD'S FLOOR IS DERIVED FROM THE STATE THAT NEEDS IT. `minHeight: 80`
existed so a thin pre-roll card would not read as cramped, but the state it
serves is the DAMAGE step, which carries no target and shows the dice notation
alone: 22 × 1.30 = 28.6 of content inside 22 of chrome, a natural 50.6 — so 80
reserved ~29pt of blank. It is now 64, which keeps ~13pt of clearance beyond the
padding. The attack prompt is content-driven at ~72pt and never touches the
floor, and no post-roll state comes near it.

THE SUITE'S JOB IS THE CONSERVATION HALF, not the reduction. Anyone can make a
panel shorter by deleting something, and that is exactly what the owner refused,
so §A proves every piece of information is still rendered — including the
advantage shadow die, the SKILL CHECK header, and the next-roll/resolving
wording — and §B pins every protected size, weight, letter-spacing, colour,
border and radius by name. Only then does §E ask whether it got smaller. §D
restates the forensic finding as a rule: this component may never acquire a
viewport, scale or device-name dependency, because a fix keyed to a phone would
be a different defect.

  ota1879TheRollLeavesRoomToRead   28/28 — composition, information, protected
                                   typography and palette, ROLL + auto-resolve +
                                   cancel, hitSlop arithmetic, device
                                   independence, per-phase derived totals,
                                   spacing bands, peak reduction, landing-jump
                                   match, sparse reservation, neighbour contracts
  related + named contracts        12 suites, 222/222 (1694, 1695, 1379, 1803,
                                   1878, 1564, 1643, 1441, 1246, 1255, 1799)
  fast surface                     1378/1378 suites · 16,078 passed · 3 skipped
  typecheck:ci                     exit 0
  typecheck:tests                  OK — at baseline (196), no growth
  lint                             clean
  check gates                      22/22

THE SUITE'S OWN FIRST DRAFT GREW THE TEST-TYPECHECK RATCHET to 199, on three
strict null checks in its helpers. They were fixed IN THE SUITE — a named guard
for the ROLL control and one for the cancel link — and the baseline was not
touched. It is still 196 and this package contributes zero to it.

ONE STRUCTURAL ADDITION, AND IT RENDERS NOTHING. `DICE_ROLLER_STYLES` exports the
StyleSheet so the geometry assertions can read the live values instead of parsing
this file's text — a regex can be satisfied by a comment, and a suite whose whole
claim is arithmetic should not be one of those. No code path reads it.

THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, none committed, each restored byte-identical. NC1
restore the old loose spacing — 5 red, all of them the proportionality section.
NC2 give the container a window-derived minimum — red on the device-independence
rule and nothing else, which is the point: the reduction tests would have stayed
green while the defect class came back. NC3 change one protected font size — red
on the typography pin; and remove the verdict line — red on the information pin.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED. `diceResults` is a row with no `flexWrap`, so a high-count
damage roll (repeater × crit × shots-per-round) can overflow the card's width —
a different axis and a different package. The structural reason the transcript
absorbs all of this is still OTA-179's sacrificial-feed ruling, which OTA-1878's
reader exists to survive; this reduces the pressure before that safety net is
needed and does not touch it.

⚠ AND ONE PROCESS ERROR, RECORDED BECAUSE THE RECEIPT WOULD OTHERWISE READ ODDLY.
The first authoritative run was launched as a bare `jest`, which runs the HEAVY
simulations too — 1388 suites in 2,501s rather than the fast surface's 1378 in
608s. It came back with one red, `playerWalkerSim`, which the repo's own
heavy-suites list names as heavy: non-required and non-gating by standing policy,
not diagnosed here, and not used as a gate. The run above is the correct surface,
`test:ci:fast`, with heavy excluded.

NOT CLAIMED: PHYSICAL VISUAL ACCEPTANCE. The geometry contract is proven by test.
Whether the tightened card LOOKS right on the owner's hardware is his call and
has not happened.
